'''Giuseppe Bruno''' (1828–1893) was an Italian [[mathematician]], professor of [[geometry]] in the [[University of Turin]].

== Life and work ==
Bruno has born in a very poor family, but he won a stipend to study in the [[University of Turin]], where he graduated in philosophy in 1846. The following years he was professor at secondary level, while he studied to graduate in engineering (1850) and to doctorate in mathematics (1851).<ref>{{smallcaps|Marchisotto & Smith}}, page 68.</ref>

In 1852 he was appointed substitute professor of mathematics in the university of Turin; he combined this work with his private and public teaching in lower levels.<ref>{{smallcaps|Segre}}, page 429.</ref> In 1862 he was appointed professor of geometry in the university; in 1881 he became president of the Sciences Faculty.<ref>{{smallcaps|Segre}}, page 430.</ref>

Bruno wrote twenty one-papers, all but two in [[geometry]], but he is mostly known by his teaching.<ref>{{smallcaps|Marchisotto & Smith}}, page 68.</ref> Among his students are [[Giuseppe Peano]] and [[Corrado Segre]].
